content.title: 3 Stocks Under $10 We Think Twice About
content.summary: Stocks trading in the $1-10 range are generally smaller players with less risk than their penny stock counterparts. But that doesn’t mean the underlying businesses are cheap, and we advise caution as many have questionable fundamentals.

content.title: 3 Reasons to Avoid SSP and 1 Stock to Buy Instead
content.summary: E.W. Scripps’s 16.3% return over the past six months has outpaced the S&P 500 by 6.5%, and its stock price has climbed to $3.98 per share. This was partly due to its solid quarterly results, and the run-up might have investors contemplating their next move.

content.title: 1 Cash-Producing Stock with Exciting Potential and 2 We Find Risky
content.summary: While strong cash flow is a key indicator of stability, it doesn’t always translate to superior returns. Some cash-heavy businesses struggle with inefficient spending, slowing demand, or weak competitive positioning.

content.title: E.W. Scripps rejects Sinclair's $622 million takeover bid
content.summary: The move follows a defensive step Scripps took in late November, when it adopted what is commonly known as a poison pill.

content.title: 3 Small-Cap Stocks with Warning Signs
content.summary: Small-cap stocks can be incredibly lucrative investments because their lack of analyst coverage leads to frequent mispricings. However, these businesses (and their stock prices) often stay small because their subscale operations make it harder to expand their competitive moats.

content.title: 1 Momentum  Stock for Long-Term Investors and 2 Facing Challenges
content.summary: The stocks in this article are all trading near their 52-week highs. This strength often reflects positive developments such as new product launches, favorable industry trends, or improved financial performance.

content.title: E.W. Scripps (SSP) Stock Trades Up, Here Is Why
content.summary: Shares of media, broadcasting, and digital services company E.W. Scripps (NASDAQ:SSP) jumped 6.9% in the afternoon session after the company received an unsolicited acquisition proposal from Sinclair, Inc. for $7.00 per share. The offer consisted of $2.72 in cash and $4.28 in Sinclair common stock for each Scripps share.
